1. SYNOPSIS
Name of Sponsor/Company:

Ocugen, Inc.

11 Great Valley Parkway

Malvern, PA 19355
Name of Investigational Product:
OCU410
Name of Active Ingredient:
Adeno-associated viral vector 5 human RORA (AAV5-hRORA)
Protocol Number:
Country:
US
Phase:
Title of Study:
A Phase 1/2 Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of OCU410 for Geographic Atrophy Secondary to Dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD).
Study Center(s):

Up to fourteen clinical study centers in the US.

PHASE 1
Study Design and Methodology:

Phase 1 is a multicenter, open-label, dose-ranging/dose-escalating study that will enroll up to 18 subjects.

A 3+3 design will be used for sequential dose-escalation cohorts in which subjects will receive a single subretinal injection of OCU410 in the study eye on Day 1.
Study Objectives:
Primary Safety:
To assess the safety of a single unilateral subretinal administration of OCU410 in subjects with Geographic Atrophy (GA) secondary to dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD).
Secondary Safety:
To assess changes in ocular safety parameters; to assess humoral and cellular immune responses to OCU410 and viral vector shedding.
Exploratory:
To assess change in prospectively collected functional and structural ocular parameters and quality-of-life measures.
Exploratory Imaging Endpoint:

EZ-RPE Structural Biomarkers

High-resolution SD-OCT images will be analyzed using validated deep learning-based algorithms to derive quantitative Ellipsoid Zone (EZ) and Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE) parameters as biomarkers of outer retinal integrity. Evaluated parameters include EZ and RPE thickness, loss/preserved areas, and EZ/RPE coupling
ratios, which correlate with photoreceptor function, disease progression, and treatment response in GA.

blocks.text: The following algorithm will be followed for dose-escalation Phase 1 study:
container_path: The following algorithm will be followed for dose-escalation Phase 1 study:

blocks.text:
Cohort 1 Low Dose (2.5x1010 vg/mL): 3 subjects will receive a subretinal injection 200 uL of OCU410 low dose concentration. The Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will review 2 weeks of safety data post-dosing and if none of the 3 subjects on low dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), then the dose will be escalated to medium dose concentration for the next cohort. In the event of a DLT, the algorithm of DLT (de-escalation or addition of 3 subjects) will be followed.

The Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will also review 4 weeks of safety data post-dosing. 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

1. If none of the first 3 subjects on low dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), then the dose will be escalated to medium dose concentration for the next cohort.

2. If 2 or more of the first 3 subjects on low dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

3. If exactly 1 of the first 3 subjects on low dose concentration is determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then 3 additional subjects will be enrolled on low dose concentration.

a) If none of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be escalated to medium dose concentration for the next cohort.

b) If 1 or more of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

Cohort 2 Medium Dose (5×1010 vg/mL): 3 subjects will receive a subretinal injection 200 uL of OCU410 medium dose concentration. The Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will review 4 weeks of safety data post-dosing.

The DSMB will review two weeks safety data after dosing the first subject in cohort 3. If there are no dose-limiting toxicities observed, Phase 2 dosing will begin simultaneously with subsequent subjects in Cohort 3. In the event of a DLT, the algorithm of DLT (de-escalation or addition of 3 subjects) will be followed.

blocks.text:
1. If none of the first 3 subjects on high dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the high dose will be determined to be the maximum tolerated dose (MTD).

2. If 2 or more of the first 3 subjects on high dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

3. If exactly 1 of the first 3 subjects on high dose concentration is determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then 3 additional subjects will be enrolled on high dose concentration.

a) If none of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the high dose will be determined to be the MTD.

b) If 1 or more of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

The DSMB will provide recommendations on proceeding to Phase 2 study at either the targeted dose, proceeding at an adjusted dose, increasing the cohort size, adding a cohort, or stopping further cohort administration if stopping criteria/criterion have been met.

The DSMB will continue to review the safety data for all enrolled subjects at the completion of the 3- month, 6-month, 9-month, and 12-month visits.

Under this design, there will be 9 subjects enrolled if there are no DLTs and up to 18 subjects under the condition that exactly 1 of the 3 subjects of every cohort is determined to have a DLT.

blocks.text: Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT) is defined as an OCU410 related event not resolving within 14 days (despite active treatment or management of the clinical condition). It is the responsibility of the investigator to assess causality. For example, one of the potential cases of DLT could be a decrease of 20 letters or more in BCVA. If DLT occurs in two subjects within same dosing cohort, the dose will not be escalated. If the BCVA decline is due to the disease's natural progression, it will not be considered a DLT

blocks.text:
Subjects who meet all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria are eligible for study participation.

1. If both eyes meet inclusion criteria, the eye with worse Best Corrected Visual Acuity (BCVA) will be established as the study eye.

2. In the case that both eyes have the same BCVA, then the right eye will be established as the study eye.

blocks.text: Inclusion Criteria:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
1. Subjects 50 years of age or older.

2. Willing and able to provide written informed consent.

3. BCVA of approximately 21 letters or more using Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) chart (20/320 Snellen Equivalent).
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text: 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
a) Total GA area ≥2.0 and ≤ 20.5 mm2 (1 to 8 disk areas [DA], respectively)

b) If GA is multifocal, at least one lesion must be ≥1.25 mm 2 (0.5 DA), with the overall aggregate area of GA as specified above in 4.a

c) The entire GA lesion must be completely visualized on the macula-centered image and must be able to be imaged in its entirety, and not contiguous with any areas of peripapillary atrophy.

5. GA lesion within foveal and perifoveal region.

6. Sufficient ocular media clarity, pupillary dilation, and subject cooperation to permit acquisition of good quality retinal imaging.

7. Subjects with liver enzyme level ≤ 1.5 x ULN.

8. Presence of any pattern of hyper-autofluorescence in the junctional zone of GA.

9. Subjects who had prior treatment with an approved drug for AMD, e.g. Izervay® (Avacincaptad pegol) or Syfovre® (Pegcetacoplan injection) can be included, after a washout period of at least 3 months in study eye. Subjects can receive an approved drug for AMD in the fellow eye, if required.

10. Subjects with history of participation in another interventional clinical study, use of any experimental treatment for AMD or any other investigational new drug, can be included after a wash out period of 3 months.

blocks.text: Note: Subject inclusion will be determined by Sponsor upon reviewing subjects screening packet, PI recommendations and in consultation with scientific advisory board (SAB). Dosing eye recommendations for surgery will be made by PI and study surgeon by reviewing screening packet and on a case-by-case basis. This recommendation will be approved by the Sponsor. Dosing eye determination can be made prior or on the day of the surgery, by evaluating the latest Ophthalmic examinations, medical history, FAF and SD-OCT images.

blocks.text: Exclusion Criteria:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
1. Previous treatment with a gene-therapy or cell therapy product

2. GA due to causes other than AMD such as Stargardt disease, cone rod dystrophy or toxic maculopathies like Plaquenil maculopathy. However, benign conditions of the vitreous or peripheral retina are not exclusionary (i.e., pavingstone degeneration).

3. Spherical equivalent of the refractive error demonstrating > 6 diopters of myopia or an axial length >26 mm, inability to fixate, uncontrolled glaucoma, advanced cataract, corneal abnormalities, medium haze, and other retinal pathologies.

4. Any history or current evidence of exudative ("wet") AMD including any evidence of retinal pigment epithelium rips, branch retinal artery or vein occlusion, corneal transplant, or evidence of neovascularization anywhere in the retina based on fluorescein angiogram.
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text: Note:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
If a subject is diagnosed with wet AMD in the study eye or fellow eye at any point during the study, they will remain part of the study and must continue to follow the assessment schedule as outlined in the protocol.

5. Any ophthalmologic condition that reduces the clarity of the media and that, in the opinion of the Investigator, prevents adequate imaging of the retina and interferes with ophthalmologic examination (e.g., advanced cataract or corneal abnormalities).

6. Have hypersensitivity to fluorescein or any contradiction for subretinal injection.

7. Aphakia, Cataract surgery or any other intraocular surgery (including lens replacement surgery) within 3 months (prior to Screening), YAG capsulotomy within 1-month, and any ophthalmic condition that may require surgery during the study period.

8. History of uveitis or endophthalmitis or laser therapy in the macular region.

9. Considered unsuitable by the Investigator for any reason including medical or psychiatric that may either place the subject at increased risk during participation or interfere with the interpretation of the study outcomes after reviewing medical, ocular, and psychiatric history, clinical examination, and laboratory evaluation (i.e., ≥ 1.5 times upper limit normal [ULN] or > 2-fold elevation of serum creatinine, etc.)

10. Have a history of stroke, heart attack or any significant cardiovascular event within 1 year prior to study participation These criteria and determination for study inclusion will be made per site PIs recommendation and on a case-by-case basis.

11. Medical or psychiatric conditions that, in the opinion of the Investigator, make consistent follow-up over the treatment period unlikely, or in general a poor medical risk because of other systemic diseases or active uncontrolled infections.

12. Any screening laboratory value (hematology, serum chemistry or urinalysis) that in the opinion of the Investigator is clinically significant and not suitable for study participation.

13. Females of child-bearing potential: Pregnancy, breast-feeding or inability to practice strict contraception within the study period (Section 8.4.2)

blocks.text: Study Design and Methodology:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
Phase 2 is a randomized dose-expansion cohort in which subjects will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive either the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) from Phase 1, or to receive a lower dose to be determined based on the safety profile from Phase 1, or to an untreated control group. A total of up to 51 subjects will be enrolled in the dose-expansion phase.

In the dose-expansion phase of the study, subjects will be randomized 1:1:1 to either two OCU410 dose groups (n=17 per group) or to an untreated control group (n=17).

Subjects who are enrolled in the untreated control group of the study will not receive any treatment. They will be followed according to the same treatment schedule as the treated subjects.

blocks.text: Sample Size Justification:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text: Assuming a two-sided alpha level of 10%, a sample size of up to 51 subjects in the expansion phase (n=17 in each of the two OCU410 dose groups and n=17 in the control group) provides 80% power to detect a 50% slowing of the GA rate in the study eye at 1 year. The GA growth rate in the control group and in each of the OCU410 dose groups were assumed to be 0.33 mm/yr, 0.165 mm/yr, and 0.165 mm/yr, respectively (SD = 0.2). The maximum total sample size across the study is 60 subjects.

2. If both eyes meet inclusion criteria, the eye with worse Best Corrected Visual Acuity (BCVA) will be established as the study eye. In the case that both eyes have the same BCVA, then the right eye will be established as the study eye.

Diagnosis and Main Criteria for Inclusion:

blocks.text: Inclusion Criteria:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
1. Subjects 50 years of age or older.

2. Willing and able to provide written informed consent.

3. BCVA of approximately 21 letters or more using Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) chart (20/320 Snellen Equivalent).
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text: 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
a) Total GA area ≥2.0 and ≤ 20.5 mm2 (1 to 8 disk areas [DA], respectively)

b) If GA is multifocal, at least one lesion must be ≥1.25 mm 2(0.5 DA), with the overall aggregate area of GA as specified above in 4.a

c) The entire GA lesion must be completely visualized on the macula-centered image and must be able to be imaged in its entirety, and not contiguous with any areas of peripapillary atrophy.

5. GA lesion within foveal and perifoveal region.

6. Sufficient ocular media clarity, pupillary dilation, and subject cooperation to permit acquisition of good quality retinal imaging.

7. Subjects with liver enzyme level ≤ 1.5 x ULN.

8. Presence of any pattern of hyper-autofluorescence in the junctional zone of GA.

9. Subjects who had prior treatment with an approved drug for AMD, e.g. Izervay® (Avacincaptad pegol) or Syfovre® (Pegcetacoplan injection) can be included, after a washout period of at least 3 months in study eye. Subjects can receive an approved drug for AMD in the fellow eye, if required.
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text: 10. Subjects with history of participation in another interventional clinical study, use of any experimental treatment for AMD or any other investigational new drug, can be included after a wash out period of 3 months.

blocks.text: Subject inclusion will be determined by Sponsor upon reviewing subjects screening packet, PI recommendations and in consultation with scientific advisory board (SAB). Dosing eye recommendations for surgery will be made by PI and study surgeon by reviewing screening packet and on a case-by-case basis. This recommendation will be approved by the Sponsor. Dosing eye determination can be made prior or on the day of the surgery, by evaluating the latest Ophthalmic examinations, medical history, FAF and SD-OCT images.

blocks.text: Exclusion Criteria:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
1. Previous treatment with a gene-therapy or cell therapy product

2. GA due to causes other than AMD such as Stargardt disease, cone rod dystrophy or toxic maculopathies like Plaquenil maculopathy. However, benign conditions of the vitreous or peripheral retina are not exclusionary (i.e., pavingstone degeneration).

3. Spherical equivalent of the refractive error demonstrating > 6 diopters of myopia or an axial length >26 mm, inability to fixate, uncontrolled glaucoma, advanced cataract, corneal abnormalities, medium haze, and other retinal pathologies.

4. Any history or current evidence of exudative ("wet") AMD including any evidence of retinal pigment epithelium rips, branch retinal artery or vein occlusion, corneal transplant, or evidence of neovascularization anywhere in the retina based on fluorescein angiogram.

If a subject is diagnosed with wet AMD in the study eye or fellow eye at any point during the study, they will remain part of the study and must continue to follow the assessment schedule as outlined in the protocol.

5. Any ophthalmologic condition that reduces the clarity of the media and that, in the opinion of the Investigator, prevents adequate imaging of the retina and interferes with ophthalmologic examination (e.g., advanced cataract or corneal abnormalities).

6. Have hypersensitivity to fluorescein or any contradiction for subretinal injection.

7. Aphakia, Cataract surgery or any other intraocular surgery (including lens replacement surgery) within 3 months (prior to Screening), YAG capsulotomy within 1-month, and any ophthalmic condition that may require surgery during the study period.

8. History of uveitis or endophthalmitis or laser therapy in the macular region.

9. Considered unsuitable by the Investigator for any reason including medical or psychiatric that may either place the subject at increased risk during participation or interfere with the interpretation of the study outcomes after reviewing medical, ocular, and psychiatric history, clinical examination, and laboratory evaluation (i.e., ≥ 1.5 times upper limit normal [ULN] or > 2-fold elevation of serum creatinine, etc.)

blocks.text: Duration of Treatment:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
Phase 1

Subjects who meet the eligibility criteria will be enrolled and will receive a single subretinal injection of OCU410 in the study eye on Day 1.

Phase 2: Subjects who are enrolled in the treatment group in Phase 2 portion of the trial will receive a single subretinal injection of OCU410 in the study eye as the subjects enrolled in Phase 1.

Subjects who are enrolled in the untreated control group of Phase 2 portion of the study will be followed for the same treatment schedule as the treatment subjects.

blocks.text:
· Screening Period (up to 90 days)

· Treatment Period (Investigational Product (IP) administration on Day 1)

· Treatment Observation Period (up to 1 year after IP administration on Day 1)

The assessments and measurements will be performed according to the Schedule of Assessments (Table 3).

Subjects are considered to have completed this study if they complete the End of Study (EOS) visit at month 12 after administration of IP. The study duration will be approximately 15 months for each subject (Screening through EOS visit).

Subjects randomized to the control group will be offered the opportunity to receive the study drug following database lock.

After the Phase 2 portion of the study has been unblinded and the full complement of safety and efficacy results have been evaluated, subjects in the control group may, at the discretion of the sponsor, enroll in an expansion protocol and receive the OCU410 treatment, provided they still meet all study eligibility criteria.

blocks.text: Statistical Methods:
container_path: 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

blocks.text:
Primary Safety Endpoints

Adverse events (AEs) will be summarized using descriptive methods including counts and percentages by eye, dosage level, MedDRA classifications, severity, and relationship to study procedures; AEs will be defined as ocular or non-ocular for presentation.

Secondary Safety Endpoints

Secondary safety endpoints and the humoral and cellular immune response (anti-AAV5 antibodies, T-cell response) to OCU410 will be summarized using summary statistics, including minimum, 1st quartile, median, 3rd quartile, maximum, mean, and standard deviation.

Primary Efficacy Endpoint

Summary statistics, graphical displays, and statistical modeling approaches will be used as applicable to evaluate efficacy endpoints across timepoints, dosage levels and eye.

All tests are two-tailed with the type I error set at 10%. GA growth rates will be square-root transformed prior to analysis. The primary comparison of interest is the difference in the mean GA growth rates across both OCU410 dose groups versus the untreated control group at 1 year.

The mean growth rates of the individual OCU410 dose groups will be compared to controls and to each other. The type I error for these comparisons will be controlled using Tukey's HSD test. Growth rates and other continuous ophthalmic measures will be analyzed using a mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) methodology with treatment, time, and time by treatment considered as fixed factors and baseline value as a covariate. An unstructured covariance assumption will be used to model the within-subject correlation. Baseline values will be centered to their mean prior to inclusion in the model. The estimated mean change from baseline to 2, 4, 12, 24, and 48 weeks along with the respective 95% confidence intervals (CI) will be calculated from the model.

Exploratory Endpoints

Continuous ophthalmic measures will be analyzed in a similar manner as described for GA lesion size. The relative risk for conversion from dry to wet AMD will be computed along with its 95% CI.

blocks.text: 4. INTRODUCTION
4.1. Disease Background

Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) is an ocular disease where macular degeneration occurs.1 It is the leading cause of blindness globally,2 affecting almost 200 million people worldwide,3 and is the leading cause of irreversible sight loss in the elderly population (adults older than 65 years) in the United States.4 Within developed countries, it is the leading cause of severe vision loss in adults 50 and older28. In 2019, an estimated 19.8 million Americans aged 40 and older were living with AMD. Its prevalence increases with age from 2% among those aged 40 to 44 years to 46.6% among those 85 years and older.5 Main risk factors for AMD include age, alcohol consumption, and smoking;6 additional risk factors include increased body mass index (BMI), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, ethnicity, and genetics.2

AMD manifests in two forms that are not mutually exclusive, as some patients with dry AMD may eventually develop wet AMD:1

1. Dry (nonexudative, atrophic) AMD: characterized by retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) dysfunction, photoreceptors loss and retinal degeneration; accounts for 85% to 90% of all AMD cases.

2. Wet (exudative, neovascular) AMD: characterized by choroidal neovascularization with intraretinal or subretinal leakage, hemorrhage and RPE detachments; accounts for 10% to 15% of all AMD cases.

Geographic atrophy (GA) is an advanced stage of dry AMD that affects nearly 1 million people in the US and 5 million people worldwide, with its prevalence increasing exponentially with age.7 It leads to progressive and irreversible loss of visual function due to the growth of atrophic lesions that destroy the retinal cells responsible for vision. GA is typically bilateral (affecting both eyes) in which both the rate and nature of GA progression are highly variable among individuals.8

The growing atrophic lesions are characterized by thinning and loss of RPE cells, photoreceptors and choriocapillaris.8 They typically first appear in the parafoveal region (noncentral GA) of the retina, affecting driving and low-light vision, and over time often expand and coalesce to include the fovea (central GA), taking approximately 2.5 years to do so.9 Once GA lesions impact the fovea, they can profoundly affect patients' reading and central vision, and subsequently affect quality of life.8
4.2. Clinical Needs

Currently, the only U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved treatment for dry AMD is Syfovre® (Apellis Pharmaceuticals) intravitreal injection indicated for the treatment of GA10, for which the Phase 1 trial evaluated safety in subjects ≥ 65 years old (NCT03777332) and the Phase 2 trial evaluated safety and efficacy in subjects ≥ 50 years old (NCT02503332)28 Syfovre® was only proven to reduce the rate of GA lesion growth at 24 months by up to 22% after monthly treatment and only by up to 18% with treatment given every other month.11 In addition, there was no clinically meaningful difference observed in visual function at 24 months.12 Importantly, in clinical trials, use of Syfovre was associated with increased rates of neovascular (wet) AMD or choroidal neovascularization. By 1 year, 12% of patients developed

neovascular AMD when administered Syfovre monthly28. This indicates that there is still a significant unmet clinical need for the majority of patients with GA, as a greater impact on slowing GA progression must be targeted, and preservation of visual function must be addressed.
4.3. Therapeutic Rationale

Ocugen, Inc. has developed a modifier gene therapy platform using nuclear hormone receptors (NHRs), which play a critical role in modulating cellular homeostasis.13-15 The modifier gene therapy platform is a new way of addressing a genetic disease arising through a multitude of genetic mutations in various genes but leading to the same end result (phenotype) of a diseased condition. A modifier gene alters the phenotype irrespective of the underlying genetic mutation causing the disease. OCU400 (a gene therapy containing hNR2E3) is another modifier gene therapy developed by Ocugen, Inc., intended to cure retinal degeneration caused by multiple gene mutations by influencing the expression of NR2E3 protein.16

While many genetic mutations and single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) have been associated with increased risk of developing dry AMD, specific genetic mutations have not been identified.

As such, OCU410 (AAV5-hRORA), is Ocugen, Inc.'s second modifier gene therapy product. OCU410 is an Adeno-Associated Virus serotype 5 containing human retinoid-related orphan receptor alpha (RORA). It is intended to treat dry AMD by delivering modifier gene RORA to photoreceptor cells and thereby influencing expression of RORA protein. Retinoid acid receptor-related orphan receptor alpha (RORA) is an NHR which is shown to impact multiple biological processes, such as development, metabolism, circadian cycle, and energy homeostasis, and plays a crucial role in lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and anti- inflammatory mechanisms1,13-15 that are critical for pathogenesis and progression of dry AMD. The role of RORA in regulating these gene pathways strongly suggests OCU410 could restore the homeostasis in the eye and thereby serve as a therapeutic candidate for dry AMD.

In pre-clinical studies, OCU410 rescued retinal degeneration and improved retinal morphology and function in Abca4- - mice. The Abca4 -- mouse is a model of the autosomal recessive Stargardt disease that shares common pathology with dry AMD (Allikmets et al., 1997; Koenekoop, 2003; Weng et al., 1999). Mutations in the ABCA4 gene lead to faulty processing and transportation of all-trans retinaldehyde from photoreceptors to the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). The disease associated with mutations in this gene is characterized by formation of auto fluorescent N-retinylidene-N-retinyl-ethanolamine (all-trans retinol) and the deposition of lipofuscin between the photoreceptor outer segments and the RPE (Cideciyan et al., 2004).

OCU410 was administered by subretinal injection into Abca4 -- mice at low (1 x 108) mid, 1 × 109), and high (4 × 109) vg/eye and mice were evaluated for therapeutic efficacy. Animals were injected at one month of age to treat at early disease state. The efficacy of these dose treatments was evaluated both functionally and structurally, and the injection improved clinical, functional, and histological outcomes with each dose. OCU410 rescued retinal degeneration for all doses, with mid and high doses showing the greatest effect. Additionally, the treatment showed no overt evidence of toxicity or abnormal structural changes in the retinas of treated mice or in the untreated contralateral eyes. Overall, administration of OCU410 via subretinal

injection attenuates retinal degeneration in Abca4- - mice at all doses with similar efficacy. The data demonstrates that AMD-like retinal degeneration can be effectively treated with OCU410 as a therapeutic.

In vitro studies in different inflammation and oxidative stress models demonstrated that OCU410 rescued both microglial and RPE cells from inflammation and oxidative stress, the two major hallmarks for dry AMD.

Ocugen, Inc., has developed a proprietary gene therapy product, OCU410, as the second agent in a novel class of NHR-based gene modifier therapy for patients with dry AMD. The proposed indication for OCU410 (AAV5-hRORA) is for the treatment of GA secondary to dry AMD.

The drug product is a sterile ophthalmic suspension for subretinal injection.

OCU410 is an adeno-associated virus serotype 5-based vector containing the human RORA gene in an expression cassette comprised of: a) AAV2 inverted terminal repeat (AAV2 ITR); b) the cytomegalovirus (CMV) enhancer; c) the chicken beta actin (CBA) promoter; d) chimeric intron; e) the cloned cDNA coding for human RORA (Retinoic Acid Receptor-Related Orphan Receptor Alpha) protein; f) the SV40 polyadenylation (PolyA) region; and g) inverted AAV2 ITR (Figure 1).

blocks.text: 4.5. Previous Study Findings
4.5.1. Nonclinical
Detailed data are described in the IB. In summary, our pre-clinical studies demonstrated a crucial role for the nuclear hormone receptor RORA in regulating multiple biological processes,

such as development, metabolism, circadian cycle, and energy homeostasis, and plays an important role in lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and anti-inflammatory mechanisms1,13-15 that are critical for pathogenesis and progression of dry AMD.
4.5.2. Clinical

OCU410 has not been previously administered to human subjects and clinical data are not available. The Phase 1/2 trial described herein represents the first-in-human (FIH) administration of OCU410. Investigators must use the safety data obtained in the nonclinical evaluation of OCU410 as the basis for informing the risk/benefit balance when selecting subjects for study participation. The IB should be read and understood in its entirety, inclusive of the Guidance for the Investigator section of the IB.

AMD is a complex multifactorial disease whose pathogenesis is incompletely understood. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the SYFOVRETM (Pegcetacoplan injection) for the treatment of geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and it is commercially available, although the reimbursement cycle has not been clarified, and official codes for the medication have not been assigned. Combining the OAKS and DERBY populations, the overall reduction of GA lesion growth ranges between 17% and 21% at 2 years with every other month and monthly dosing, a clinically meaningful but modest effect29. The adverse reactions including vitreous floaters, conjunctival hemorrhage, vitreous detachment, retinal hemorrhage, punctate keratitis, posterior capsule opacification, and increased intraocular pressure have been reported in patients treated with SYFOVRE™M Importantly, in clinical trials, use of Syfovre was associated with increased rates of neovascular wet AMD or choroidal neovascularization. By 1 year, 12% of patients developed neovascular AMD when administered Syfovre monthly. Overall, there is still unmet medical need for dry AMD patients. Therapeutic intent for OCU410 is both functional as well as structural.
4.6. Clinical Rationale
4.6.1. Rationale for Study Design

The study is designed to evaluate the safety of ascending dose levels of OCU410 in a stepwise, sequential manner in a small number of subjects. Ongoing evaluation of emergent safety data will be conducted by the Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB). The design includes discrete study periods that allow subjects' screening, enrollment, treatment, and measurements of outcomes. Multiple factors are incorporated into the study design to safeguard and monitor the rights and safety of subjects and are described herein.

To maximize subject protection, the study will be conducted by Investigators at clinical sites with expertise in retinal diseases and advanced therapies such as gene therapy. All sites will be carefully evaluated and pre-qualified prior to study participation. Sites will have experience in FIH studies with gene therapy and appropriate training and equipment on site for emergency management, if required. All sites will be trained on the Protocol and all study procedures, including surgical procedure for dose administration to ensure compliance and the protection of subject safety and rights. All investigative sites have experience in subretinal injections for administration of gene therapy and the procedure will be standardized across centers.

The number of subjects included in the trial minimizes the number of subject exposures while providing a sufficient dataset to allow a preliminary clinical assessment of OCU410's safety profile within the dosage range evaluated. OCU410 will be administered in one eye (study eye) of each subject. Administration of escalating doses of OCU410 is completed via discrete cohorts. A minimum of 4 weeks will elapse between dosing of cohorts to allow for peak expression of the transgene, immune response and for review of the emergent safety data.

The DSMB will conduct ongoing review of emergent safety data from the study and make recommendations on study progression. Criteria are established for dose adjustments and for cohort and study stopping. Adjustments to target doses and the number of subjects per cohort may be recommended based on review of the data. If DLTs occur in two subjects within the same dosing cohort, the dose will not be escalated.

The assessments and measurements in the trial assess both general systemic safety and ocular safety. Baseline is established for subjects and intensive monitoring of subject safety in the days and weeks following dose administration is incorporated. Intermediate and long-term monitoring is incorporated in the first-year post-dose Treatment Observation Period.
4.6.2. Rationale for Dose, and Duration of Treatment
container_path: 4.6.2. Rationale for Dose, and Duration of Treatment

blocks.text:
OCU410 has been evaluated in a nonclinical program to demonstrate proof of concept (POC), safety and immunogenicity in non-clinical models. The results support the further evaluation of OCU410 in humans.

In vivo pharmacology studies in mice for OCU410 established minimum effective dose (MED). Additionally, we considered the maximum tolerable dose (MTD) in nonhuman primate (NHP) eye, which is the ideal non-clinical model for the human eye. Based on these calculations, the highest clinical doses for Phase 1/2 trials were selected.

It is important to note that we have an ongoing clinical trial of another modifier gene therapy OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) that targets retinitis pigmentosa and Leber congenital Amaurosis (LCA) (NCT05203939). We observed preliminary positive signal for efficacy with no safety concern even after 6 months with a clinical dose of 1 X 1010 Vg/eye. OCU410 is also AAV5 based therapy and it is therefore reassuring that the planned clinical doses would be useful from both efficacy and safety standpoints.

blocks.text: Selection of the starting dose:
container_path: 4.6.2. Rationale for Dose, and Duration of Treatment

blocks.text:
The dose of OCU410 is defined based on both the vector genome (vg) and the subretinal injection volume (microliter, uL). Two dose-levels will be sequentially tested.

The starting dose of vector genome (vg) is selected based on preclinical animal experiments, including preclinical efficacy studies in mice and the toxicology studies in large animals.

Injection volume is selected 200 uL. Current subretinal injection protocols use a volume ranging from 100 µL (e.g., XIRIUS Study17), 200 µL (e.g., TIGER Study18), to 300 uL (Luxturna Study19,20, OCU400-101 Study). Currently, with the FDA approval of Luxturna®, 300 uL is the most commonly used volume. Under the vitrectomy setting and well-controlled injection speed, these volume ranges are proven to be safe. The choice of volume is dependent on the target treatment regions of the retina. The XIRIUS study and TIGER Study both aim to treat the central retina with an injection volume range from 100-200 uL while Luxturna® aims
container_path: 4.6.2. Rationale for Dose, and Duration of Treatment

blocks.text:
to treat pericentral retina. It was trialed and later approved to be used with a 300 uL injection volume.

Therefore, 200 uL volume was chosen for OCU410 subretinal injection. As in the surgical settings, the injection volume may vary at the surgeon's discretion, considering safety and beneficiary treatment coverage.

The surgeon must take priority for the protection of the fovea and the aimed treatment area according to pre-operative imaging studies; therefore, the locations and numbers of retinotomy, and the total volume may vary. However, 200 uL of volume per eye is required. Multiple injection sites are allowed to deliver the desired volume. Since only a single dose of OCU410 will be administered during the study, no treatment discontinuation is expected.

blocks.text: 4.6.3. Risks and Benefits

OCU410 Risks

The results of toxicology studies and efficacy in multiple relevant animal models strongly support OCU410 as a potential treatment option for GA in humans. The study described herein is designed to evaluate the safety and tolerability of OCU410 at multiple target doses.

Since OCU410 has not been previously administered to humans, unidentified risk may not be known at this time. More detailed information about known and expected risks and reasonably expected adverse events of procedures may be found in the IB, which is the single reference safety documents for this study It is important the Investigator thoroughly read and understand the IB for OCU410 and use the data presented in the IB as the basis for risk assessment in subjects. If additional safety information becomes available during the trial, it will be provided to Investigators and subjects.

Subretinal Injection Risks

Risks associated with subretinal injection include pain, cataract formation, endophthalmitis, corneal changes, intraocular hemorrhage (subretinal, vitreoretinal and suprachoroidal), increased IOP, intraocular inflammation, retinal breaks, retinal detachments, hypotony, scleritis, uveitis or sympathetic uveitis and decrease or loss of vision.22,23

Risks associated with nerve block (sub-tenon, retrobulbar or peribulbar) may include globe perforation, retrobulbar hemorrhage, optic nerve damage, subconjunctival edema, venous and arterial hemorrhage, decreased visual acuity, and myotoxicity.24 Systemic risks may include subarachnoid injection causing respiratory arrest; seizures, loss of consciousness and respiratory depression or cardiac arrest associated with systemic toxicity; pulmonary edema, reaction to epinephrine; oculocardiac reflex and vasovagal reaction; and allergic reactions.24

Risks associated with general anesthesia may include nausea, vomiting, chills, short-term confusion, and sore throat from breathing tube insertion.25 Rare and serious risks may include postoperative cognitive dysfunction with long-term memory and learning problems; malignant hyperthermia; and breathing problems during and after surgery.25

Other Procedural Risks

Venipuncture to obtain blood samples may result in bruising, inflammation, and pain. New hypersensitivity or allergic reactions (not previously observed in the subject) may occur to ocular agents used during ocular examinations. If medical adhesives are used (bandages, ECG pads, etc.) mild skin irritations and redness may occur on skin exposed to these adhesives. Hypersensitivity reactions may occur to eye drops or anesthetic and antimicrobial drops used in surgical and other ophthalmic procedures. Fatigue may be experienced when multiple ophthalmic assessments are completed during a study visit.

COVID Risks

Against the background of the COVID-19 pandemic, the potential risk of a subject developing COVID-19 has been considered in terms of the risk/benefit evaluation. The mode of action of OCU410 has been considered alongside available nonclinical data and OCU410 does not have immunomodulatory effects that would confer an increased risk to subjects enrolled in the study

either contracting or experiencing a more serious disease if infected with SARS-CoV-2. The following COVID-19 Risk Mitigation measures will be implemented:

· The Sponsor will work with clinical sites to document site-level procedures regarding COVID-related precautions for subjects and staff. These precautions may include use of personal protective equipment such as face coverings, masks, and shields, and procedures such as temperature screening and social distancing and will be consistent with the policies of the institution and compliant with government guidelines.

· The site visit schedule has been carefully reviewed to minimize unnecessary visits and minimize subject exposure. The schedule is not expected to increase subject risk beyond that encountered in the routine delivery of healthcare for subjects with chronic eye disease.

· The Sponsor will continue to assess risk during the clinical study. This risk assessment will include overall study risk as well as regional risks to allow for adaptations that may be required at a local level depending on COVID-19 infection rates across US regions and cities. Risk mitigation measures, where applicable, will be amended based on emerging government guidelines.

Benefits

This study is designed to evaluate the safety of ascending doses of OCU410 in subjects with GA secondary to dry AMD. Exploratory endpoints may provide preliminary information on the efficacy of treatment with OCU410; however, subjects may receive no benefit from participation in this study. Subjects may experience improvements in their visual acuity. Any such improvement may be transitory. Subjects may experience an altruistic sense of satisfaction by participating in this study knowing that information learned from this study may benefit others and aid in the advancement of therapeutic options for future subjects.
5. STUDY OBJECTIVES AND ENDPOINTS Phase 1 and Phase 2 Study Endpoints
5.1. Primary Safety Objective
To assess the safety of a single unilateral subretinal administration of OCU410 in subjects with Geographic Atrophy (GA) secondary to dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD).
5.2. Secondary Safety Objectives
To assess change in ocular parameters for safety; to assess humoral and cellular immune responses to OCU410 and shedding of the viral vector.
5.3. Exploratory Objectives
To assess change in prospectively collected functional and structural ocular parameters and quality-of-life measures.

6. INVESTIGATIONAL PLAN
6.1. Overall Study Design

An overview of the study design is presented in Figure 2 and the flow of the OCU410 administration by cohorts is presented in Figure 3.

Phase 1 is a multicenter, open-label, dose ranging/dose escalation study with 3 consecutive cohorts. A total of 9 to 18 subjects will be enrolled. A 3+3 design will be used for sequential dose-escalation cohorts in which each subject will receive a single subretinal injection of OCU410 in the study eye on Day 1.

Phase 2 is a multicenter, outcome assessor-blinded, expansion phase in which subjects will be randomized 1:1:1, to one of two OCU410 dose groups or to an untreated control group. OCU410 doses will include the MTD from Phase 1 and a second dose to be determined based on the safety profile.

The study schedule for an individual subject will consist of the following periods (Figure 2):

· Screening Period (up to 90 days)

· Treatment Period (IP administration on Day 1)

· Treatment Observation Period (up to 1 year after IP administration on Day 1)

blocks.text: 6.2. Number of Subjects
The maximum total sample size across the study is 60 subjects.
6.3. Treatment Assignment

Phase 1 is an open-label study, and all subjects will receive a single subretinal injection of OCU410 at the target or adjusted dose level assigned to their respective cohort. A maximum of 18 subjects will participate in Phase 1.

Phase 2 is a randomized, outcome assessor-blinded study in which subjects will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to two OCU410 treatment groups or an untreated control group. A total of up to 51 subjects will be randomized in Phase 2.
6.4. Dose Adjustment Criteria
6.4.1. Safety Criteria for Adjustment or Stopping Doses
container_path: 6.4.1. Safety Criteria for Adjustment or Stopping Doses

blocks.text:
This Protocol allows for adjustment of targeted doses based upon emergent data from ongoing DSMB safety reviews.

Common expected adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) are known complications of vitrectomy, subretinal injection, anesthesia, and corticosteroids. Details of AEs and SAEs are described in the IB.

The expected AEs include conjunctival hyperemia, vitreous or choroidal hemorrhage, RPE changes, cataract, increased intraocular pressure, dellen (thinning of the cornea), retinal tear, eye inflammation, macular hole, retinal deposit, hypopyon, eye irritation, eye pain, epiphora, and maculopathy; as well as SAEs including endophthalmitis, foveal thinning and loss of foveal function, fovea dehiscence (separation of the retinal layers in the center of the macula), retinal hemorrhage. These AEs and SAEs are frequently related to vitrectomy and subretinal injection.

Potential systemic AEs include hematuria, vomiting, nausea, pyrexia, and headache; systemic SAEs include anal fistula, paresthesia, convulsion, hyper- or hypoglycemia, leukocytosis and adverse drug reactions related to anesthesia and use of corticosteroids.

Dose-limiting side effects are defined as OCU410 related AEs that are considered severe in nature, intolerable, or that, in the opinion of the Investigator, Sponsor, or DSMB would place subjects at medical risk if a higher dose of OCU410 were to be administered. Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT) is defined as an event not resolving within 14 days (despite active treatment or management of the clinical condition). All ophthalmologic adverse events will be categorized or graded per PI's discretion and based in accordance with clinical standard of care guidelines. The dose-limiting side effects of this study are as follows:

· A decrease of 20 letters or more in BCVA.

· Persistent or new onset of intraocular inflammation beyond the post-operative Week 12, including: anterior uveitis with more than 3+ (i.e., 4+) cells in anterior chamber, intermediate vitreous cells more than 3+ (i.e., 4+), or pan-uveitis, Iritis, photopsia, ocular discomfort, ptosis, eyelid cyst, conjunctival hemorrhage, eye
container_path: 6.4.1. Safety Criteria for Adjustment or Stopping Doses

blocks.text:
pain, vitritis, and macular cyst despite adequate treatment. The grading is based on Standardization of Uveitis Nomenclature (SUN).

· Rare systemic AAV5-related coagulopathy with deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism or disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), when no other possible causes can be discovered.

If dose-limiting side effects occur within a cohort, the DSMB may make the recommendation to proceed at a lower dose in the next cohort, increase the size of the cohort, or they may recommend that no further dose-escalation occur. The DSMB will clearly document their recommendations and the rationale for the recommendations according to procedures detailed in the DSMB Charter.

blocks.text: 6.5. Criteria for Study Termination

The study may be terminated by the Sponsor at any time and for any reason after informing the Investigators. The DSMB may also recommend study termination. Study termination means the permanent stopping of administration of OCU410 to additional subjects, inclusive of subjects screened, and subjects enrolled to whom OCU410 has not yet been administered to. Termination does not mean suspension of scheduled safety monitoring procedures in the Treatment Observation period of the study.

If the study is terminated, the following instructions should be followed, unless the DSMB and/or the Study Medical Monitor advise otherwise:

7. SELECTION AND WITHDRAWAL OF SUBJECTS

Subjects meeting all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria are eligible for study participation.

If both eyes meet inclusion criteria, the eye with worse BCVA will be established as the study eye. In the case that both eyes have the same BCVA, then the right eye will be established as the study eye.
Note on Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV):
No subjects with history of CNV were excluded from participating in the study.
7.1. Subject Inclusion Criteria

1. Subjects 50 years of age or older

2. Willing and able to provide written informed consent

3. BCVA of approximately 21 letters or more using Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) chart (20/320 Snellen equivalent).
4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows:

a) Total GA area ≥2.0 and ≤20.5 mm2 (1 to 8 disk areas [DA], respectively)

b) If GA is multifocal, at least one focal lesion must be ≥1.25 mm2 (0.5 DA), with the overall aggregate area of GA as specified above in 4.a

c) The entire GA lesion must be completely visualized on the macula-centered image and must be able to be imaged in its entirety, and not contiguous with any areas of peripapillary atrophy

5. GA lesion should be within foveal and perifoveal region.

6. Sufficient ocular media clarity, pupillary dilation, and subject cooperation to permit acquisition of good quality retinal imaging

7. Subjects with liver enzyme level ≤ 1.5 x ULN

8. Presence of any pattern of hyper-autofluorescence in the junctional zone of GA.

9. Subjects who had prior treatment with an approved drug for AMD, e.g. Izervay® (Avacincaptad pegol) or Syfovre® (Pegcetacoplan injection) can be included, after a washout period of at least 3 months in study eye. Subjects can receive an approved drug for AMD in the fellow eye, if required.

10. Subjects with history of participation in another interventional clinical study, use of any experimental treatment for AMD or any other investigational new drug, can be included after a wash out period of 3 months.
Note:

Subject inclusion will be determined by Sponsor upon reviewing subjects screening packet, PI recommendations and in consultation with scientific advisory board (SAB). Dosing eye recommendation for surgery will be made by PI and study surgeon by reviewing screening packet and on a case-by-case basis. This recommendation will be approved by the Sponsor. Dosing eye determination can be made prior or on the day of the surgery, by evaluating the latest Ophthalmic examinations, medical history, FAF and SD-OCT images.
7.2. Subject Exclusion Criteria

1. Previous treatment with a gene-therapy or cell therapy product.

2. GA due to causes other than AMD such as Stargardt disease, cone rod dystrophy or toxic maculopathies like Plaquenil maculopathy. However, benign conditions of the vitreous or peripheral retina are not exclusionary (i.e., pavingstone degeneration)

3. Spherical equivalent of the refractive error demonstrating > 6 diopters of myopia or an axial length >26 mm, inability to fixate, uncontrolled glaucoma, advanced cataract, corneal abnormalities, medium haze, and other retinal pathologies

4. Any history or current evidence of exudative ("wet") AMD including any evidence of retinal pigment epithelium rips, branch retinal artery or vein occlusion, corneal transplant, or evidence of neovascularization anywhere in the retina based on fluorescein angiogram
Note:

If a subject is diagnosed with wet AMD in the study eye or fellow eye at any point during the study, they will remain part of the study and must continue to follow the assessment schedule as outlined in the protocol.

5. Any ophthalmologic condition that reduces the clarity of the media and that, in the opinion of the Investigator, prevents adequate imaging of the retina and interferes with ophthalmologic examination (e.g., advanced cataract or corneal abnormalities)

6. Have a hypersensitivity to fluorescein or any contradiction for subretinal injection

7. Aphakia or Cataract surgery within 3 months, YAG capsulotomy within 1-month, other intraocular surgery (including lens replacement surgery) within 6 months (prior to Screening), and any ophthalmic condition that may require surgery during the study period

8. Have a history of uveitis or endophthalmitis or laser therapy in the macular region

9. Considered unsuitable by the Investigator for any reason including medical or psychiatric that may either place the subject at increased risk during participation or interfere with the interpretation of the study outcomes after reviewing medical, ocular, and psychiatric history, clinical examination, and laboratory evaluation (i.e., ≥ 1.5 times ULN or > 2-fold elevation of serum creatinine, etc.)

10. Have history of stroke, heart attack or any significant cardiovascular event within the last 1 year prior to study participation. This criteria and determination for study inclusion will be made per site PIs recommendation and by a case by case basis.

11. Medical or psychiatric conditions that, in the opinion of the investigator, make consistent follow-up over the treatment period unlikely, or in general a poor medical risk because of other systemic diseases or active uncontrolled infections

12. Any screening laboratory value (hematology, serum chemistry or urinalysis) that in the opinion of the Investigator is clinically significant and not suitable for study participation.
Note:

If laboratory screening tests are out of local laboratory normal ranges and deemed clinically significant, repeat of screening tests is permitted once during the screening period to assess eligibility.
13. Females of child-bearing potential:
Pregnancy, breast-feeding or inability to practice strict contraception within the study period (Section 8.4.2)
Males:
Sperm donation or inability to practice strict contraception within the study period (Section 8.4.2)
Note:
Apart from the above-mentioned criteria, subject eligibility will be determined by the sponsor on a case-by-case basis.
7.3. Subject Withdrawal Criteria

Subjects may be withdrawn from the study for any of the following reasons:

1. A subject is free to withdraw informed consent from the study at any time, without prejudice to further treatment the subject may need to receive.

2. Withdrawn at the discretion of the Investigator for safety, behavioral, compliance, or administrative reasons. This is expected to be uncommon.

At the time of discontinuation from the study, if possible, an early discontinuation visit should be conducted. All assessments outlined for early withdrawal visit should be completed. In the event that a subject elects not to return to the clinic for the scheduled visit, the Investigator must make every effort to contact the subject to review all AEs.

If a subject has an adverse event, the subject will be followed until the adverse event has either resolved or satisfactorily stabilized in the judgment of the Investigator.

When a subject withdraws from the study because of an SAE, the SAE must be recorded on the electronic case report form (eCRF) and reported on the clinical trial SAE Report. Subjects who have been treated with OCU410 will be encouraged to remain in the study and complete all safety follow up assessments.

If the subject withdraws consent for disclosure of future information, the Sponsor may retain and continue to use any data collected before such a withdrawal of consent. If a subject withdraws from the study, he/she may request destruction of any remaining samples, but data already generated from the samples will continue to be available and may be used to protect the integrity of existing analyses. The Investigator must document any such requests in the site study records.

Every effort should be made to encourage subjects withdrawing from the study to complete the early withdrawal assessments listed in the Schedule of Assessments (Table 3). Likewise, every effort to determine the reason for withdrawal should be made and the reason for withdrawal recorded in the eCRF.

If a subject withdraws from the study after enrollment, but before receiving a dose of the IP then follow-up beyond the Screening evaluations is not required.

Any subject to whom OCU410 has been administered and who is discontinued for an adverse event will not be replaced. A subject who is withdrawn from the study during the Screening and Baseline periods before administration of OCU410 may be replaced at the discretion of the Sponsor.
7.3.1. Lost to Follow-Up

Subjects will be considered lost to follow-up (LTFU) if they repeatedly fail to return for scheduled visits without stating an intention to withdraw consent and they cannot be contacted by the study site. The following actions must be taken if a subject fails to return to the clinic for a required study visit:

· The site must attempt to contact the subject and reschedule the missed visit as soon as possible, counsel the subject on the importance of maintaining the assigned visit schedule and ascertain whether the subject wishes to and/or should continue in the study.

· Before a subject is deemed lost to follow up, the Investigator or designee must make every effort to regain contact with the subject (where possible, 3 telephone calls and, if necessary, a certified letter to the subject's last known mailing address or local equivalent methods). These contact attempts (e.g., dates of telephone calls and registered letters) should be documented in the subject's medical record. A subject should not be considered LTFU until these efforts have been made.

· Should the subject continue to be unreachable, he/she will be considered to have withdrawn from the study.

blocks.text: 8.2. Pre- and Post-Operative Therapy
8.2.1. Pre- and Post-Operative Oral Prednisone

Subjects scheduled for subretinal injection of OCU410 will take an orally administered systemic corticosteroid (prednisone) at a dose and regimen prescribed by the Investigator. Prednisone will be given orally at 1mg/kg/day (maximum dose of 80 mg/day) starting 3 days prior to injection and continued for a total of 10 days, followed by 0.5 mg/kg/day tapered over 6 weeks. The regimen for systemically administered prednisone is provided herein with deviations allowed at the Investigator's discretion, i.e., adjustments in oral prednisone can be done per standard of care at the discretion of the Investigator (calcium, vitamin-D, GI prophylaxis with antacids, H2 blockers or PPIs (proton pump inhibitors) are permitted when prescribing the high dose prednisone).
8.2.2. Pre- and Post-Operative Injection of Sub-Tenon Triamcinolone Acetate
container_path: 8.2.2. Pre- and Post-Operative Injection of Sub-Tenon Triamcinolone Acetate

blocks.text: Subjects scheduled for subretinal injection of OCU410 will be given sub-tenon triamcinolone 40 mg per discretion of the Investigator prior to surgery. Sub-tenon injection on the day of surgery is allowed. A repeat injection of sub-tenon triamcinolone 40 mg can be considered at the responsible PI and/or surgeon's discretion, i.e., adjustments in injection of sub-tenon triamcinolone can be done per standard of care at the discretion of the Investigator after a 6-week interval.
container_path: 8.2.2. Pre- and Post-Operative Injection of Sub-Tenon Triamcinolone Acetate

blocks.text: 8.2.3. Post-Operative Topical Corticosteroid Use

Post-operatively, prednisolone acetate 1.0% (or dexamethasone 0.1%, or equivalent), four times daily (QID) for 1 week, decrease by 1 drop per week for 3 weeks (total of 4 weeks) will be prescribed by the Investigator.

Adjustments in corticosteroid use can be done per standard of care at the discretion of the Investigator. All administration of systemic and/or topical corticosteroids will be recorded as concomitant medications.
8.2.4. Post-Operative Antibiotic Use

After subjects receive subretinal injection of OCU410, topical 1% atropine eyedrops twice daily (BID) and antibiotic drops (moxifloxacin unless contraindicated by allergy) four times daily (QID) for one week will be prescribed. Adjustments in antibiotic use can be done per standard of care at the discretion of the Investigator.
8.3. Other Clinical Supplies

Ocugen, Inc. or designee will provide materials required for preparation and administration of the OCU410 solution. This includes diluent, syringes, needles, and vials required for dilution and the sterile syringes, needles, and subretinal cannula required for injection. Instructions for the preparation and administration of OCU410 are provided in the Pharmacy Manual and are to be followed explicitly.
8.4. Concomitant Medications and Procedures

Medications taken within 4 weeks prior to Screening will be recorded in the eCRF.

Concomitant medications (prescription, over the counter (OTC), or herbal) are to be administered with discretion from Screening until 3 months following administration of IP unless they are prescribed by the Investigator for treatment of specific clinical events or in association with the surgical administration of OCU410 and study assessments. Concomitant medications administered in association with the surgical administration of OCU410 are to be prescribed per standard of care at the discretion of the Investigator. Any prohibited or contraindicated medications should not be administered to trial subjects (Section 8.4.1).
Exceptions apply to Investigator approved medications taken by the subject for ongoing or chronic health conditions and include the following:

blocks.text: · Use of fluorescein drops, dilation eyedrops, anesthetic eyedrops and microbial eyedrops are allowed for ocular procedures and will be recorded in the eCRF.
container_path: Exceptions apply to Investigator approved medications taken by the subject for ongoing or chronic health conditions and include the following:

blocks.text:
· Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors (CAIs) at a stable dose and regimen.

· Use of contraceptives (see Section 8.4.2).

· Local corticosteroids administered, as specified by the Protocol.

· Oral anticoagulants that are not newly prescribed and which have been administered at the same dose and regimen for 4 weeks prior to dose administration.

· Hypertensive medications that are not newly prescribed and which have been administered at the same dose and regimen for 4 weeks prior to dose administration.

· Other non-retinotoxic medications required for the treatment or management of health conditions during the treatment and follow-up period.

· GI prophylaxis with antacids, H2 blockers or PPIs.

A concomitant procedure is any therapeutic intervention (e.g., surgery/biopsy, physical therapy) or diagnostic assessment performed between the time the subject enrolled (at Screening) and last study visit. Concomitant procedures must be recorded in the eCRF.

AEs related to administration of concomitant therapies or procedures must be documented on the appropriate eCRF.
8.4.1. Prohibited Medications

· Investigational agents other than OCU410.

· High dose (>7500 retinol equivalent units or >3300 IU) per day of vitamin A.

· Tretinoin-containing skin cream (e.g., Retin-A).

· Isotretinoin.

· Viagra (sildenafil) or related compounds used to treat erectile dysfunction.

· Hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, mellaril, or any related retino-toxic compounds.
8.4.2. Contraception

· Female subjects who are postmenopausal must have had no menstrual bleeding for at least 1 year and either be > 60 years old or have an elevated plasma follicle-stimulating hormone level > 40 mIU/mL at Screening.

· Female subjects of childbearing potential (i.e., ovulating, pre-menopausal, and not surgically sterile) must have a documented negative pregnancy test at intervals throughout the study according to the Schedule of Assessments (Table 3).

· Female subjects of childbearing potential must use a highly effective method of contraception (i.e., <1% failure rate) during the study period (until EOS visit). Acceptable methods of contraception for female subjects enrolled in the study include the following:

- Surgical sterilization (tubal ligation)

- Abstinence

- Intrauterine device for at least 12 weeks (about 3 months) before Screening.

- Hormonal contraception (oral, implant, injection, ring, or patch) for at least 12 weeks before Screening.

- Diaphragm used in combination with spermicide.

· All male subjects (unless surgically sterile) must use a highly effective method of contraception (i.e., <1% failure rate) during the study period (until EOS visit). Acceptable methods of contraception for male subjects enrolled in the study include the following:

- Condoms with spermicide.

- Surgical sterilization (vasectomy) at least 26 weeks before Screening.

- Male subjects must agree to abstain from sperm donation during the study period (until EOS visit).
8.5. Treatment Compliance

OCU410 is administered as a single subretinal injection. Compliance will be assessed by review of site IP receipt and accountability records and subject dose administration records. Deviation(s) from the prescribed dosage regimen should be recorded in the eCRF. The vial lot number, dose, and injection time are monitored and recorded by the site staff. Therefore, full compliance with OCU410 injection is anticipated.
8.6. Randomization and Masking

The Phase 1 portion of the study will be non-randomized and open label.

Subjects in Phase 2 will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to either one of two OCU410 dose groups or an untreated control group. Ocular assessments in Phase 2 will be outcome assessor-blinded. A blinding plan will be developed that will ensure that the clinical outcome evaluators operate in a completely blinded manner during the Phase 2 portion of the study.
8.7. Study Drug Materials and Management

An overview of OCU410 presentation, use and management is provided here. Detailed procedures for obtaining, storing, preparing, and administering the Study Drug (SD) are provided in the Pharmacy Manual which must be used in conjunction with this Protocol.
8.8. Study Drug

OCU410 is an adeno-associated virus (AAV) serotype 5-based gene therapy vector. It consists of a human RORA gene in an expression cassette comprised of: a) AAV2 inverted terminal repeat (AAV2 ITR); b) the cytomegalovirus (CMV) enhancer; c) the chicken beta actin (CBA) promoter; d) chimeric intron; e) the cloned cDNA coding for human RORA protein; f) the SV40 polyadenylation (PolyA) region; and g) inverted AAV2 ITR (see Figure 1 and Section 4.4).

Please refer to the IB for a full description of the drug product.
8.9. Study Drug Packaging and Labeling

OCU410 will be provided to the clinical site as OCU410 DP kit that contains One (1) 2-mL crystal zenith (CZ) vial of OCU410 DP and three (3) 2-mL crystal zenith (CZ) l vials of diluent (formulation buffer). DP is provided as 0.5 ml extractable volume whereas diluent is provided in as 1.5 ml extractable volume in the CZ vials. The supplied concentration requires dilution prior to administration. All drug products will be labeled according to FDA 21 CFR 312.6.

Please reference the Pharmacy Manual for procedures to order the SD.
8.10. Study Drug Storage

OCU410 must be stored in a secure location with access limited to designated study personnel. Storage temperature must be compliant with that stated on the drug label. Records of continuous temperature monitoring of the drug storage area must be available for inspection by study monitors and the Sponsor. If the required temperature storage conditions are exceeded, the temperature excursion must be reported immediately following the procedures provided in the Pharmacy Manual.
8.11. Study Drug Preparation

OCU410 must be properly diluted prior to administration to subjects for all dose concentrations. Directions for the preparation are detailed in the Pharmacy Manual and must be followed explicitly. Ocugen, Inc. evaluated the in-use stability and device compatibility of OCU410 DP for the doses prepared for administration for nonclinical studies. The results show that the dosing apparatus did not impact the intended dose concentration, and the product is stable up to 8 hours at 2-8℃ and room temperature(~23℃).
8.12. Administration

OCU410 is administered by subretinal injection. Procedures for administration are provided in the Surgical Manual and must be followed explicitly. Only retinal surgeons trained on OCU410 administration technique may perform the subretinal injections. The designated retinal surgeons must be listed on the delegation of authority log with their role(s) clearly defined.
8.13. Study Drug Accountability

The Investigator is accountable for maintaining timely, complete, and accurate records of the request, receipt, storage, use and return of all SD. These records must always be available for inspection by study monitors and the Sponsor. Full details for SD accountability are provided in the Pharmacy Manual and must be followed explicitly.
8.14. Study Drug Handling and Disposal

OCU410 must be stored in a secure area according to storage conditions specified on the drug product label. It is the responsibility of the Investigator to ensure that the drug product is dispensed for use only in study subjects. OCU410 must only be dispensed from official study sites by authorized personnel.

Disposal of SD at the study pharmacy (used vials and residual OCU410 not administered or wasted in priming) may be permitted after confirmation of adequate site policies and procedures for disposal of cell and gene therapy products and upon written authorization from Ocugen, Inc. Any unused vials of SD remaining at the end of the study will be disposed of at study completion. Procedures for final accountability and final disposition of SD and associated materials are provided in the Pharmacy Manual.
9. ASSESSMENT OF SAFETY
9.1. Safety Parameters

All subjects receiving OCU410 will be included in the safety summary. Safety will be assessed by medical review of AE reports, clinical laboratory findings, physical examinations, vital signs, ophthalmic examination, humoral and cellular response to OCU410, and vector shedding.

Safety assessments are to be conducted according to the Schedule of Assessments provided in Table 3. Brief descriptions of each of the safety parameters are provided herein.
9.1.1. Demographics
Demographic information including age, gender, ethnicity, and race will be obtained at the Screening visit.
9.1.2. Medical History

A full medical history and comprehensive ocular history will be obtained at the Screening visit. Medical history should focus on recent history with an emphasis on the history of GA and any associated ocular procedures and/or medications. The comprehensive ocular history will include diagnostic data, diagnosis, and disease progression as documented through medical notes and results of ophthalmic exams, procedures, and assessments.
9.1.3. Vital Signs

All vital sign measurements will be taken after a subject has been in a sitting position for a minimum of 5 minutes. Vital signs will include systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, respiration rate, and body temperature. Radial or brachial pulse will be measured over a 30 second interval, if performed manually and respiration rate will be measured over a 60 second interval. Body temperature may be oral or aural. Blood pressure should be obtained from the same arm throughout the study whenever possible. An electronic or manual sphygmomanometer or an electronic oscillometric device may be used. The method of assessment should be consistent throughout the study.
9.1.4. Height and Weight

Height and weight will be measured in full indoor clothing without shoes at specific visits according to the Schedule of Assessments (Table 3). A body-mass index (BMI) will be calculated using the Screening height and weight values.
9.1.5. Physical Examination

Physical examination assesses the general wellness of the subject. Report any acute distress, pain, or discomfort with focused system examination if the subject is symptomatic. The Investigator determines if an emergency referral or referral to a specialist is needed. A full physical examination is required at the Screening of subjects and at regular intervals according to the Schedule of Assessments (Table 3). The physical examination includes skin, ENT, head, chest, abdomen, musculoskeletal, and extremities.
9.1.6. Laboratory Assessments

A listing of laboratory tests utilized during the Screening Period to qualify subjects for study participation and throughout the study to monitor subject safety is provided in Table 6. All laboratory testing will be conducted in the fasting state and a CLIA certified central laboratory will be used for all analyses. Blood and urine samples are to be obtained and processed according to instructions provided in the Study Reference/Lab Manual. Investigators will review all laboratory reports in a timely manner and assess all values outside the reference ranges for clinical significance.

The Investigator must review the laboratory report, document this review, and record any clinically relevant changes occurring during the study in the AE section of the eCRFs. The laboratory reports must be filed with the source documents. Clinically significant abnormal laboratory findings are those which are not associated with the underlying disease, unless judged by the Investigator to be more severe than expected for the subject's condition.

All laboratory tests with values considered clinically significantly abnormal during participation in the study should be repeated until the values return to normal or baseline or are no longer considered clinically significant by the Investigator or medical monitor.

If such values do not return to normal/baseline within a period of time judged reasonable by the Investigator, the etiology should be identified, and the Sponsor notified.

All protocol-required laboratory assessments, as defined in Table 6, must be conducted in accordance with the laboratory manual and the Schedule of Assessments (Table 3).

If laboratory values from non-protocol specified laboratory assessments performed at the institution's local laboratory require a change in subject management or are considered clinically significant by the Investigator, then the results must be recorded in the eCRFs.
